newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek econ ministry optimistic on stock market.
newsitem.headline: Greek econ ministry optimistic on stock market.

text.p: National economy ministry general secretary Apostolos Fotiadis said on Thursday the stock market's recent rise was perfectly normal and the favourable conditions for its further growth were well in place.
Political stability, the successful course of the pursued economic policy, the drop in inflation and interest rates contributed to the market's rally, he told reporters.

Fotiadis was reacting to a warning from capital market commission president Stavros Thomadakis after the markets closed on Wednesday that recent continuous advances had worried the commission as they could give rise to speculative conditions.

"Wednesday's statement by the capital market commission president aimed to caution retail investors who massively entered the bourse. To warn them to be careful in their investment choices," Fotiadis said.
But other national economy ministry sources told Reuters that Thomadakis had acted without the prior knowledge of national economy minister Yannos Papandoniou.
Thomadakis issued a statement on Thursday morning denying that he would resign over the furore.
"Overall, all the preconditions for the stock market's continued positive course have been secured," Fotiadis said.

Greek shares lost 5.95 percent or 86.44 points after panic selling brought the benchmark index down to 1,367.16 points on Thursday on heavy volume of 30.8 billion drachmas. The index fell more than 7.0 percent during the session.
